items.description: Welcome to this month’s AWS Security news! Organizations need current information about AWS Security developments to maintain their cloud security. items.title: Secure agentic access to AWS with Enterprise-Managed Authorization
items.description: AWS Sign-In is introducing support for Enterprise-Managed Authorization (EMA) using the Identity Assertion JWT Authorization Grant (ID-JAG), enabling organizations to securely authorize AI agents to access AWS MCP Server through their existing enterprise identity providers (IdPs), such as Okta. With this capability, organizations can centrally manage which applications can access Amazon Web Services (AWS) resources […]

items.title: Reduce operational overhead by migrating from AWS CloudHSM to AWS KMS
items.description: AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) supports the security certifications, algorithms, and performance that most AWS CloudHSM workloads require. Organizations that migrate from AWS CloudHSM to AWS KMS have significantly reduced costs while eliminating hardware security module (HSM) provisioning, patching, and high-availability management. For a detailed comparison of both services, see AWS KMS or AWS […]

items.description: Amazon Cognito handles sign-in and access control for users, AI agents, and microservices with managed user directories, social and enterprise federation, and passwordless sign-in with passkeys or one-time passwords. items.title: Introducing context-aware rules for AWS Network Firewall
items.description: AWS Network Firewall now supports context-aware rules, which match traffic by the AWS resources that send and receive it instead of by IP address. A rule can name a virtual private cloud (VPC), a subnet, a security group, or a transit gateway attachment. Rules that match on IP addresses have to keep up with every […]

items.title: Introducing AWS Network Firewall Next Generation policy
items.description: When it comes to inspecting network traffic, many security teams want two things from a firewall. They want to allow only the traffic each application needs, and they want each allowed connection checked for known threats. Today, you can do both with AWS Network Firewall, a stateful, managed network firewall and intrusion detection and prevention […]

items.title: AWS Network Firewall introduces automated internet firewall mode (Preview)
items.description: AWS Network Firewall now offers automated internet firewall mode (Preview). In this mode, Network Firewall applies your centrally defined rules to traffic at the internet gateway of each of your virtual private clouds (VPCs). It also performs built-in network address translation (NAT) for outbound-only connections. A subnet that reaches the internet needs only one route, […]

items.description: Suppose you use a restaurant review app to check reviews, book tables, and email invitations to your friends. items.description: Today, AWS is making it easier to grant access and audit activity based on the user or workload (a non-human caller, such as an application, service, or an automated workflow) behind an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role. items.description: When you build AI agents, you often want each agent or sub-agent to have only the permissions its tasks require, rather than the full permissions of the session that started it.
